title: Condorcet Winner Probability and Noise Stability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to a sign. Choose a ranking profile uniformly from all profiles of $n$ voters, and let the Condorcet winner probability be the probability that the societal outcome has a Condorcet winner. Then this probability equals $\frac34-\frac34\operatorname{Stab}_{-1/3}(f)$, where $\operatorname{Stab}_{-1/3}(f)$ is the expected product of the real-valued outputs of $f$ on a uniformly random sign vector and a second vector obtained by independently retaining each coordinate with probability $1/3$ and flipping it otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional sign cube to a sign
